columns.rationale: Two-letter IATA carrier code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 across 16 rows (values such as "9E", "AA", "DL", "WN"), so it is fully populated and unique per row.
Airline display name with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 (for example "Delta Air Lines Inc.", "Virgin America"), kept as VARCHAR because the values are free-form proper names.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; the 16 distinct UUID-shaped capture identifiers (e.g. "06a98b09-9d5f-7d1f-8000-66033e8441d3") carry no business meaning.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 1 with min = max = "2026-09-02T23:26:17" records only the capture time of this load.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; distinct_count 1 with the single value "{}" carries no business content.

decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 over row_count 16, so bronze contains no exact duplicate rows and no dedupe step is proposed.

carrier has distinct_count 16 over row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, making it the smallest fully populated column that identifies one row; name is equally distinct (16) but is a free-form label rather than a code.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata: true and are dropped; _airbyte_extracted_at and _airbyte_meta each have distinct_count 1, so no lineage information is lost within this load.
Both business columns landed as VARCHAR and their distinct_values are codes and proper names with no numeric or ISO-timestamp shape, so no cast is justified by the samples.
carrier and name each report null_count 0 and null_rate 0.0, so both are proposed required with null_handling not_applicable.

purpose: silver_airlines is the cleaned lookup of airline carriers landed from bronze.nyc_airlines, mapping each two-letter IATA carrier code to its full airline name. It feeds joins from flight-level fact tables that carry only the carrier code.
usage: Join on carrier, the declared grain, to attach a human-readable airline name. The table is a small reference dimension of 16 rows; name is a display label and should not be used as a join key. No pipeline metadata columns remain, so downstream consumers cannot derive load timestamps from this table.
limitations: Cleanup only dropped the three Airbyte capture columns and renamed nothing; no casts, dedupe, or derived flags were applied because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 and both business columns are text with no numeric or temporal shape. The profile covers only 16 rows from a single extraction (_airbyte_extracted_at distinct_count 1), so the uniqueness of carrier should be re-measured against the full warehouse table before the grain is approved. The profile carries no evidence about whether carrier codes are ever retired or reused over time.
